notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated reserved GPU pools with multi-region failover and measurable SLA guarantees. Customer is a consumer analytics platform (personalization + post-purchase support) with strict latency and residency constraints.

Workload profile and targets: steady-state throughput target ~120 requests/sec (chat-oriented), expected 95th percentile token length ~220 tokens, burst planning up to 500 req/sec during peak campaigns, embeddings jobs scheduled nightly (batch windows). Latency SLOs: p95 < 120ms for short-context assistant calls, p99 target < 350ms across single-region traffic; negotiating a p99 300ms contractual SLO for critical support routes. Cost sensitivity: wants clear unit economics per 1M tokens and optional quantized model tiers to trade cost vs. quality.

Reserved GPU pool planning (current ask):
- Primary region: us-west-2 pool reserved: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs dedicated to their account (expected to sustain 120 req/s with continuous batching).
- Secondary region: us-east-1 pool reserved: 2x A100-80GB-equivalent as active-active for routing and capacity smoothing.
- EU failover: eu-west-1 warm-standby 1x A100-80GB reserved for data-residency-critical traffic; only route EU traffic to EU pool.
- Failover headroom: ask for ~30% headroom above steady-state reserved capacity to handle AZ failure + short-term bursts (e.g., reserve multiplier 1.3).
- AZ distribution: prefer 2 AZ spread per region to avoid single-AZ loss; ask Redwood to specify recommended AZ placement for best isolation.
- Autoscale policy: prefer reserved baseline + quick burst capacity (burst pool) for 10-15 minute windows; fallback policy should route to lower-cost quantized variant when capacity constrained.
- Warm-up and caching: KV cache population expected to take 3-5 minutes per model variant after failover; require documentation on cache pre-warm strategies and recommended long-lived keep-alive patterns.

POC / evaluation plan: 2-week dedicated soak test, synthetic traffic generator with 80/20 chat/embeddings split, run sustained 4-hour windows at 120 req/s and several 30-min 500 req/s spikes. Success criteria: no p99 regressions beyond agreed tolerance, <1% error rate, autoscale transitions within committed times. Redwood to supply perf profile for selected model family (quantized and fp16 variants) and recommended batching configuration.

SLA negotiation points currently open: uptime target (customer requests 99.95% for Dedicated), financial credits calculation for breach, RTO for cross-region failover (customer requests <60s for routing switch), cache RPO (how much state is recoverable post-failover), telemetry retention for 90 days, and explicit data residency clauses for EU traffic.

Security/compliance: must integrate with Lighthouse SSO (SAML IdP), use customer-managed KMS for key encryption, and provide SOC2 + pen-test artifacts. Audit logs and token-level billing required for internal chargeback. Legal has flagged data residency language for EU customers — Redwood draft term needs modification.

Commercial/ops notes: procurement prefers committed monthly reserved plan with optional burst credits billed on usage. Pricing sensitivity around A100 80GB-equivalent hourly rate vs. quantized TPU/GPU alternatives. Requesting an itemized SOW that lists per-region reserved counts, failover headroom formula, escalation contacts, and clear SLAs for latency and uptime.

Next steps (short): 1) Capacity-sizing workshop w/ Redwood infra lead (Marco) week of 2026-03-15. 2) Lighthouse to provide model list + token distribution by 2026-03-18. 3) Redwood to deliver draft SOW & pricing by 2026-03-25. 4) Legal to review revised residency clause before procurement sign-off.
